exposure: Intrathecal 1% 2-chloroprocaine (30 mg) with fentanyl (25 mcg) as an adjuvant
outcome: Time to achieve block height (T10, T6)
Adverse effects (hypotension, bradycardia, nausea, vomiting, pruritus, shivering, sedation, respiratory depression)
cohort: The study included one hundred parturient (50 in each group) with term pregnancy (>=36 weeks), ASA physical status II, aged 18-35 years, scheduled for low-risk elective caesarean section under subarachnoid block (SAB).
finding: Intrathecal 2-chloroprocaine with fentanyl as an adjuvant significantly prolongs the duration of sensory blockade and postoperative analgesia compared to 2-chloroprocaine alone, with similar motor blockade and complication rates in patients undergoing elective lower segment caesarean section.
cross-section timing: The retrospective data collection spanned 6 months.
